description: Network connections, IPsec, network authentication, certificate services, and network-related security activity.

source.note: Events from Certificate Services, NPS, Wired/Wireless, and Plug-and-Play providers appear in their own channels — display provider and channel with the event.

4825.headline: A user was denied access to Remote Desktop
4825.plain_english: Someone was denied access to Remote Desktop. Repeated denials can indicate someone trying to guess RDP credentials.
4825.technical_description: Security event 4825: access to Remote Desktop was denied by policy or logon restriction.
4825.why_it_matters: Repeated RDP denials from unknown sources can be early password-guessing indicators.
suspicious_when: Repeated denials for the same user
what_to_do: Check whether the source IP is expected
Correlate with 4625 and 4624 LogonType 10

severity.high: Repeated denials from unfamiliar external sources

4825.important_note: Repeated RDP denials from an external IP often indicate scanning or guessing.

4886.headline: Certificate Services received a certificate request
4886.plain_english: The certificate authority received a request for a new certificate.
4886.technical_description: Security event 4886: Certificate Services received a certificate request.

who.SubjectUserName: Account that submitted the request, if recorded

4886.why_it_matters: Unexpected certificate requests can indicate abuse of AD Certificate Services (ESC attacks).
what_to_do: Check the requested template and requestor
Correlate with 4887 for issuance
4886.important_note: AD CS abuse is a common privilege-escalation path — check templates.

4887.headline: Certificate Services approved and issued a certificate
4887.plain_english: The certificate authority approved a certificate request and issued a certificate.
4887.technical_description: Security event 4887: Certificate Services approved a request and issued a certificate.
4887.why_it_matters: Issuance of certificates with authentication capabilities can enable account impersonation.
suspicious_when: Issuance for a template that allows authentication (Client Authentication, Smartcard Logon)
what_to_do: Confirm the certificate was requested by the owner
Review the template

severity.high: Issuance from a sensitive authentication template

4887.important_note: Certificates from auth templates are equivalent to credentials.

4888.headline: Certificate Services denied a certificate request
4888.plain_english: The certificate authority denied a certificate request.
4888.technical_description: Security event 4888: Certificate Services denied a certificate request.
4888.why_it_matters: Repeated denials from unusual accounts can indicate a certificate-abuse attempt.
what_to_do: Check the requestor and template
Correlate with other CA events

severity.high: Denials from unusual account or template

4888.important_note: Denials can be the only trace of a failing abuse attempt.

4893.headline: Certificate Services archived a key
4893.plain_english: The certificate authority archived a private key. This is a sensitive operation because archived keys can be recovered.
4893.technical_description: Security event 4893: Certificate Services archived a key.
4893.why_it_matters: Archived keys can be recovered later; unexpected archives are sensitive.
what_to_do: Confirm the archive was expected
Check who has key-recovery permissions
4893.important_note: Key recovery permissions are highly privileged — audit them separately.

4898.headline: Certificate Services loaded a template
4898.plain_english: The certificate authority loaded a certificate template.
4898.technical_description: Security event 4898: Certificate Services loaded a template.
4898.why_it_matters: Template changes can introduce new abuse paths.
what_to_do: Confirm the template load was expected
Review the template's permissions
4898.important_note: Template permissions are a common AD CS abuse vector.

5136.headline: A directory service object was modified
5136.plain_english: An Active Directory object was modified. AD is the directory that stores users, computers, and permissions — changes to objects can grant access.
5136.technical_description: Security event 5136: a directory service object was modified. Includes ObjectDN, AttributeLDAPDisplayName, and old/new values.

where.Computer: Domain controller that recorded the change

5136.why_it_matters: AD object changes are the primary means of privilege escalation in Windows domains.
suspicious_when: Change to adminSDHolder, ACLs on privileged objects, or msDS-AllowedToActOnBehalfOfOtherIdentity
what_to_do: Review which attribute changed and to what
Correlate with 4624 and 4672

severity.high: Change to sensitive ACLs or properties

5136.important_note: Changes to ACLs on privileged objects are high-value — investigate carefully.

5137.headline: A directory service object was created
5137.plain_english: A new object (user, computer, group, OU) was created in Active Directory.
5137.technical_description: Security event 5137: a directory service object was created.

target.ObjectDN: Distinguished name of the new object

where.Computer: Domain controller that recorded the creation

5137.why_it_matters: New objects can be a persistence mechanism.
suspicious_when: Creation of a privileged object or one with admin-sounding name
what_to_do: Confirm the creation was requested
Review any subsequent changes to the new object
5137.important_note: Depends on the object type and follow-up activity.

5140.headline: A network share was accessed
5140.plain_english: Someone accessed a shared folder or file share over the network.
5140.technical_description: Security event 5140: a network share object was accessed. ShareName identifies the share.
5140.why_it_matters: File-share access can indicate legitimate collaboration or data theft.
normal_when: User accessing a shared folder they normally use
what_to_do: Confirm the account is expected to access this share
Review 5145 for specific objects

severity.high: Bulk access or access to sensitive share by unexpected account

5140.important_note: 5145 shows the specific file/folder; 5140 shows the share.

5145.headline: A network share access check occurred
5145.plain_english: Windows checked whether a user has permission to access a specific file or folder on a share. Shows which files were accessed.
5145.technical_description: Security event 5145: detailed file share access check. RelativeTargetName is the specific file/folder.
5145.when: Time Windows recorded the access check.
5145.why_it_matters: Higher fidelity than 5140 — shows exactly which files were touched.
suspicious_when: Bulk access to many files by one account in a short window
what_to_do: Review the file names accessed
Correlate with 5140 and 4624

severity.high: Bulk access or access to sensitive files

5145.important_note: Use file names to spot data-theft patterns.

5632.headline: A wireless network authentication was requested
5632.plain_english: A request was made to authenticate to a wireless network.
5632.technical_description: Security event 5632: authentication request to a wireless network.
5632.why_it_matters: Unusual SSID requests can indicate rogue access point attempts or unusual roaming.
normal_when: Connecting to a known corporate SSID
what_to_do: Check the SSID against the approved list
Correlate with device location

severity.high: Connection to a known-bad SSID or unusual pattern

5632.important_note: Wireless events are logged on the client or NPS depending on configuration.

5633.headline: A wired network authentication was requested
5633.plain_english: A request was made to authenticate to a wired network.
5633.technical_description: Security event 5633: authentication request to a wired network.
5633.why_it_matters: Unusual wired authentication can indicate a rogue device on the network.
suspicious_when: Unexpected wired auth on a normally-wireless device
what_to_do: Confirm the device is expected to be on the wired network
5633.important_note: Rogue wired devices are a network security concern.

6272.headline: Network Policy Server granted access to a user
6272.plain_english: A Network Policy Server (used for RADIUS, VPN, and 802.1X) granted access to a user.
6272.technical_description: Security event 6272: NPS granted access. Records user, calling station, policy name.
6272.why_it_matters: Unauthorized NPS grants can indicate policy misconfiguration or credential compromise.
normal_when: User connecting via VPN or 802.1X as expected
what_to_do: Confirm the user and device are expected
Check the matched policy

severity.high: Granted to a compromised or unauthorized identity

6272.important_note: NPS events depend on the RADIUS role being enabled.

6273.headline: Network Policy Server denied access to a user
6273.plain_english: A Network Policy Server denied access. Repeated denials can indicate guessing or misconfiguration.
6273.technical_description: Security event 6273: NPS denied access. Includes reason code.
6273.why_it_matters: Repeated denials can indicate guessing, misconfiguration, or unauthorised devices.
suspicious_when: Repeated denials for the same user
what_to_do: Review the reason code and source
Correlate with 4625 and 4771
6273.important_note: High volume of denials is often the first sign of credential guessing.

6278.headline: Network Policy Server granted full access to a user
6278.plain_english: NPS granted full access (as opposed to limited access). Full access may include more permissive network access.
6278.technical_description: Security event 6278: NPS granted full access.
6278.why_it_matters: Full-access grants to unexpected identities can indicate misconfiguration or compromise.
what_to_do: Confirm the identity and matched policy
6278.important_note: Check the matched policy to understand why full access was granted.

6416.headline: A new external device was recognized
6416.plain_english: A new external device (USB, Bluetooth, etc.) was connected and recognised. Useful for detecting unauthorised USB drives or peripherals.
6416.technical_description: Security event 6416: new external device recognised by the system.

where.Computer: Machine where the device was connected

6416.why_it_matters: USB devices are a common exfiltration and malware-delivery vector.
suspicious_when: Device connected by an unusual user
what_to_do: Confirm the device is authorized
Check whether data was copied after connection

severity.high: Unauthorized USB storage or device with suspicious pattern

6416.important_note: Depends on device class — USB mass storage is more sensitive.

6423.headline: A device install was blocked by policy
6423.plain_english: A device installation was blocked by policy. This can be routine (device-control policy) or a sign someone tried to install an unauthorized device.
6423.technical_description: Security event 6423: installation of a device was prohibited by system policy.

where.Computer: Machine where the install was attempted

6423.why_it_matters: Repeated blocks can indicate attempted policy bypass.
normal_when: User plugging in a non-approved USB drive
suspicious_when: Block followed by policy changes (unlikely in most orgs)
what_to_do: Confirm the attempt is a training issue vs. suspicious intent

severity.high: Block correlated with policy change or other suspicious activity

6424.headline: A previously blocked device install was allowed
6424.plain_english: A device that had been blocked was allowed to install after policy was changed. If policy change wasn't authorized, this is a red flag.
6424.technical_description: Security event 6424: installation of a previously-prohibited device was allowed.
6424.why_it_matters: Indicates policy was relaxed or bypassed — high-value signal if unexpected.
what_to_do: Confirm the policy change was authorized
Review who modified the device policy

severity.high: Policy change correlated with other suspicious activity

6424.important_note: Requires coordination with device-control policy audit.
